value.name: Asha acknowledges the corrections
value.description: Asha looks up at Rosa, nods once, and silently signals that she has completed the corrections she came to make.
evidence: looked up at Rosa for the first time since she had started, the corrected pages stacked under her hand, and gave one short nod that meant she had done what she came to the table to do

value.name: Rosa asks if Asha feels better
value.description: Rosa quietly asks Asha whether she feels better now, probing the emotional effect of the completed corrections.
evidence: Rosa drew her fingertips back from the cover, leaned into her chair, and said, quietly, do you feel better now

value.name: Asha withholds an immediate answer
value.description: Asha pauses instead of answering Rosa, revealing that the real issue is not the corrections but the unresolved question of the Tuesday signature.
evidence: Asha didn't answer right away; she set the pen down beside the stack and looked at the place on the folder where Rosa's hand had been

because the honest answer was that the corrections were the easy part and Rosa knew it, and the harder one—what to say about the Tuesday signature, and to whom—was still sitting on the table between them in ink that would be hers on Monday

value.name: Rosa presses for the truth about Tuesday
value.description: Rosa leans in and directly asks who will be told the truth about Tuesday, making the hidden issue explicit.
evidence: "Who gets the truth about Tuesday?" she asked

value.name: Asha counters with a question about witnesses
value.description: Asha avoids answering Rosa's question and instead asks who else saw the documents, shifting the issue to possible witnesses.
evidence: Asha didn't look away this time; she drew the corrected stack back toward her own side of the table, set her palm flat on the top folder where Rosa's fingertips had been, and after a moment asked, "Who else saw these?"
It was not an answer to Rosa's question

value.name: Both recognize the questions are equivalent
value.description: Rosa accepts Asha's non-answer, and both women understand that the two questions are really the same dilemma from different angles.
evidence: Rosa let it stand as not-an-answer, because the two questions were the same question approached from opposite sides, and both of them knew that whatever Asha decided about the second would decide the first

value.name: Asha reveals the Tuesday filing
value.description: Asha pulls the Tuesday filing out from under the corrected pages and places it between them, exposing the document at the center of their conflict.
evidence: Asha slid the Tuesday filing out from under the corrected stack and laid it flat between them

value.name: Asha prepares to continue handling the filing
